proof.text: Work in $\mathcal M=\operatorname{Mod}(A)$, which is Grothendieck abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-modules-grothendieck-abelian]. For every ideal $K$, the functor $\Gamma_K$ of [def-sbc-ideal-power-torsion-functor] is additive and left exact in the sense of [def-sp-left-exact-additive]: for a map $u:N\to P$, the kernel of its restriction to $\Gamma_K(N)$ consists precisely of the elements of $\ker u$ killed by a power of $K$, hence is $\Gamma_K(\ker u)$. For a finite product, a common exponent is the maximum of the finitely many exponents, so $\Gamma_K$ preserves finite products. Its action on maps is restriction of the original linear map.

proof.text: Identify $\Gamma_I(\Gamma_J(N))$ with $\Gamma_{I+J}(N)$ by the identity on underlying elements. The former consists of $x\in N$ killed by both $I^a$ and $J^b$ for some $a,b\geq1$. Expanding $(I+J)^{a+b}$ as the sum of $I^uJ^v$ for $u+v=a+b$, each summand kills $x$ because either $u\geq a$ or $v\geq b$. Conversely, $(I+J)^c x=0$ implies $I^c x=J^c x=0$ by inclusion of ideals, and thus gives an element of $\Gamma_I(\Gamma_J(N))$. These identifications commute with every module map because all maps are the restrictions specified by [def-sbc-ideal-power-torsion-functor]. This proves a natural isomorphism $\Gamma_I\circ\Gamma_J\cong\Gamma_{I+J}$, without a separate composition lemma.

source.place: Tag 0BJC (lemma-local-cohomology-ss), specialized to a module; Noetherian injective-resolution argument from Tag 0955 (lemma-local-cohomology-noetherian), using Tag 08XW (lemma-injective-module-divide)(2).

proof.text: For every injective $A$-module $E$, apply [lem-per-ideal-torsion-preserves-injectives] with $K=J$. The Noetherian hypothesis gives that $\Gamma_J(E)$ is itself an injective $A$-module. Resolve this module by itself in degree zero and zero in all positive degrees; this is an injective resolution in the sense of [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Applying $\Gamma_I$ therefore gives zero cohomology in every positive degree, by the right-derived-functor computation in [def-sbc-ideal-power-torsion-functor]. Thus $\Gamma_J(E)$ is $\Gamma_I$-acyclic by [def-sp-acyclic]. Together with Step 1 this verifies every condition of the composable pair [def-sp-composite-acyclicity], with $F=\Gamma_J$ and $G=\Gamma_I$ and with all three categories equal to $\mathcal M$.

proof.text: Apply [thm-sp-grothendieck] to this pair and the module $M$. Its functorial first-quadrant spectral sequence has $E_2^{p,q}=R^p\Gamma_I(R^q\Gamma_J(M))=H_I^p(H_J^q(M))$ and converges to $R^{p+q}(\Gamma_I\circ\Gamma_J)(M)$. To identify the latter with $H_{I+J}^{p+q}(M)$, choose the same injective resolution $M\to E^\bullet$ for both functors. The elementwise natural isomorphism of Step 2 gives an isomorphism of complexes $\Gamma_I(\Gamma_J(E^\bullet))\cong\Gamma_{I+J}(E^\bullet)$, commuting with their differentials because it commutes with every linear map. Taking cohomology identifies their derived functors using [def-sbc-ideal-power-torsion-functor]. The identification is natural: on a map of resolutions each component is the identity on the same torsion elements, and independence of resolutions is [lem-sp-derived-well-defined].

source.place: Tag 0BJC (lemma-local-cohomology-ss), specialized to a module; Noetherian injective-resolution argument from Tag 0955 (lemma-local-cohomology-noetherian), using Tag 08XW (lemma-injective-module-divide)(2).

proof.text: Unpack the convergence just supplied by [thm-sp-grothendieck], using [def-sp-convergence] and [def-sp-filtration]. For each $n\geq0$ the abutment has an exhaustive separated decreasing filtration $F^pH^n$ with $F^pH^n/F^{p+1}H^n\cong E_\infty^{p,n-p}$. The first-quadrant condition forces these quotients to be zero for $p<0$ and $p>n$. Hence the filtration is constant for $p\leq0$ and for $p\geq n+1$; exhaustivity makes the first constant value $H^n$ and separatedness makes the second zero. Thus $H^n=F^0H^n\supseteq\cdots\supseteq F^{n+1}H^n=0$ is the required finite filtration. Transport it along the natural abutment identification of Step 4. The spectral sequence and its filtration retain the functoriality in $M$ of the cited Grothendieck construction.

title: Derived-support spectral sequence for a sum of ideals
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $I,J$ be finitely generated ideals, and let $M$ be any $A$-module. Write $H_K^n(N)=R^n\Gamma_K(N)$ for the right derived functors of the ideal-power torsion functor [def-sbc-ideal-power-torsion-functor], for $K=I,J,I+J$. There is a natural convergent first-quadrant spectral sequence [def-sp-spectral-sequence] $E_2^{p,q}=H_I^p(H_J^q(M))\Longrightarrow H_{I+J}^{p+q}(M)$, where $p,q\geq0$. Convergence means that for each $n\geq0$, $H_{I+J}^n(M)$ has a finite filtration [def-sp-filtration] whose associated graded modules are $E_\infty^{p,n-p}$ for $0\leq p\leq n$.
